lab-1.title: Lab 1: RC Circuit Transient Dynamics (Experiment)
lab-1.description: Hardware experiment analyzing RC circuit step response, time constant tau, and phase lag on an oscilloscope.
lab-1.steps_and_theory:
--- LAB STEPS & PROCEDURES ---
Step 1: Wire a 1k Ohm resistor and 10uF capacitor in series across a function generator outputting 5V peak-to-peak square wave at 50Hz.
Step 2: Connect Oscilloscope Probe 1 to Channel 1 (Input V_in) and Probe 2 to Channel 2 (Capacitor voltage V_cap).
Step 3: Measure the time constant tau from 0% to 63.2% of peak voltage.
Step 4: Theoretical Q1: How does increasing resistance R affect the charging time constant tau?
Step 5: Theoretical Q2: Derive the formula for cutoff frequency f_c from the transfer function.
lab-1.model_answers:
--- TA MODEL ANSWERS ---
Step 3 Expected Value: tau = R * C = 1000 * 10 * 10^-6 = 10 ms.
Theoretical Q1 Answer: Increasing R increases tau, meaning the capacitor takes longer to charge.
Theoretical Q2 Answer: f_c = 1 / (2 * pi * R * C) = 15.91 Hz.

lab-2.title: Lab 2: Binary Search Tree Implementation (Coding)
lab-2.description: Implementation of BST insertion, search, and in-order traversal in C++/Python.
lab-2.steps_and_theory:
--- CODING LAB REQUIREMENTS ---
Task 1: Implement insert(root, value) to add nodes into the BST.
Task 2: Implement search(root, key) returning true if key exists.
Task 3: Implement inorder_traversal(root) printing values in sorted ascending order.
Theoretical Question: What is the worst-case time complexity of BST insertion, and how can a balanced tree (AVL/Red-Black) prevent it?

lab-3.title: Lab 3: Geometrical Optics - Thin Lens Focal Length & Snell's Law
lab-3.description: Optical bench experiment measuring thin lens focal length, 1/u vs 1/v graph fitting, and prism refractive index with laser.
lab-3.steps_and_theory:
==============================================================================
PHYSICS DEPARTMENT: EXPERIMENT LAB 3 SPECIFICATION
LAB TITLE: GEOMETRICAL OPTICS - THIN LENS FOCAL LENGTH & SNELL'S LAW
==============================================================================

EQUIPMENT REQUIRED:
- Optical Bench with meter scale
- Converging Biconvex Lens (L1) and Diverging Biconcave Lens (L2)
- Illumination Source (Object Arrow Pin) and White Viewing Screen
- Glass Prism and Semiconductor Laser Diode (lambda = 632.8 nm)

EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURE:
Step 1: Mount the light source at 0.0 cm mark and converging lens L1 at 50.0 cm mark.
Step 2: Adjust screen position until a sharp, inverted image of the object pin is formed. Record object distance u and image distance v.
Step 3: Repeat measurements for 5 different u positions (30cm, 40cm, 50cm, 60cm, 70cm).
Step 4: Plot 1/u vs 1/v graph. Calculate focal length f from the y-intercept (focal length formula: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v).
Step 5: Place the glass prism on the optical table. Shine the laser beam at incident angle theta_1 = 30 degrees. Measure angle of refraction theta_2 inside glass.

THEORETICAL QUESTIONS:
Q1: State Snell's Law of Refraction and explain why a ray bends toward the normal when entering an optically denser medium.
Q2: Calculate theoretical refractive index n of glass if incident angle is 45 degrees and refraction angle is 28 degrees.
Q3: What is the significance of the critical angle theta_c in Total Internal Reflection (TIR)?
lab-3.model_answers:
==============================================================================
TA MODEL ANSWERS & ANSWER KEY: EXPERIMENT LAB 3 (OPTICS)
==============================================================================

EXPECTED EXPERIMENTAL VALUES:
- Lens L1 Biconvex Focal Length: f_expected = 15.0 cm (± 0.5 cm margin of error).
- Graph 1/u vs 1/v: Slope = -1.0, Y-intercept = 1/f = 0.0667 cm^-1.

THEORETICAL ANSWERS:
Q1 Answer: Snell's Law states n1 * sin(theta_1) = n2 * sin(theta_2). Light slows down in denser media (v = c/n), so to minimize optical path time (Fermat's Principle), the ray bends toward the normal.

Q2 Answer: n = sin(45°) / sin(28°) = 0.7071 / 0.4695 = 1.506 (Refractive index of crown glass ~ 1.51).

Q3 Answer: Critical angle theta_c = arcsin(n2/n1) is the angle of incidence above which light is completely reflected back into the medium without any refraction.
